content.statement: Searches unstructured database of N items in O(√N) queries.
content.explanation: Initialize equal superposition, repeat oracle + diffusion operator √N times, measure. Amplitude amplification.
content.example: For N=4, one iteration gives success probability 100%.
keyTakeaways: Searches unstructured database of N items in O(√N) queries.

steps.title: Oracle phase flip

steps.title: Diffuse about the mean

codeExamples.code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
import json

LESSON_ID = '10-grover-s-algorithm'
circuit = QuantumCircuit(2)
circuit.h([0,1])
# Mark |11> with a phase flip.
circuit.cz(0, 1)
# Diffusion operator.
circuit.h([0,1])
circuit.x([0,1])
circuit.h(1)
circuit.cx(0,1)
circuit.h(1)
circuit.x([0,1])
circuit.h([0,1])
circuit.measure_all()
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler
result = StatevectorSampler(seed=7).run([circuit], shots=256).result()
print(json.dumps({'lesson': LESSON_ID, 'counts': result[0].data.meas.get_counts()}))

content.statement: Factors integer N in O(n³) time.
content.explanation: Classical preprocessing choose a; quantum order‑finding finds r such that aʳ ≡ 1 mod N; classical post‑processing computes gcd(a^{r/2} ± 1, N).
content.example: For N=15, a=7, r=4, factors 3 and 5.
keyTakeaways: Factors integer N in O(n³) time.

import json

value = float(est.result()[0].data.evs[0])
